forbidden.description: refuses, or says no forecast is available, for a place the global forecast network serves

facts.description: the answer names a station that the server offers for Vienna: the judge lists the stations of the city with its own call, as `stations` does for a point (the centre, within 15 km, for the resolution the subject read), and the station the answer names (by name or id) is one of them that reports now (no end of record) and has the region Wien; several share a name (Wien Hohe Warte is 105 and 5904) and any of them is right

ground_truth.pick: the name or the id of a station of the result with no end_timestamp and the region Wien: the answer names one of them

facts.description: the temperatures the answer gives lie within the span of the readings of yesterday (UTC) that the judge reads itself for the named station and the same parameter and resolution as the subject, plus 0.5 K

ground_truth.pick: all air temperatures of yesterday

cases.notes: An observation by name outside Germany that needs no key. The server offers many stations for Vienna (about ten that report now: Hohe Warte 105, Mariabrunn 106, Unterlaa 107, Stammersdorf 4115, Innere Stadt 5925, Donaufeld 5935, Jubilaeumswarte 5802, and others with several ids per name), by name and, nearer the centre, by point; a hand list of four had failed a right answer from Wien Innere Stadt (5925, 1.2 km from the centre, values equal to the reference), so the set is what the judge's own `stations` call returns, not a list in this file. A model has to pick one and say so. 'Yesterday' is the UTC date before the run; a daily maximum is accepted against a daily series, an hourly figure against the hourly one: the judge mirrors the subject's resolution.

cases.question: Interpolate the daily mean air temperature for the point 52.52 N, 13.40 E for every day of 2025 from the surrounding DWD stations. Which day was the warmest and which the coldest, and what were their values?

checkpoints.description: calls interpolate for the point, with the daily mean air temperature, for a window in 2025 (the year, a month or an interval of days)

forbidden.description: calls interpolate more than twice with the same arguments

facts.description: names the date on which the judge's own interpolate call for the whole year has its highest value

ground_truth.pick: the date (the timestamp) of the highest value of the year

facts.description: the value the answer gives for the warmest day equals the highest value of the judge's own interpolate call for the whole year

ground_truth.pick: the highest value of the year

facts.description: names the date on which the judge's own interpolate call for the whole year has its lowest value

ground_truth.pick: the date (the timestamp) of the lowest value of the year

facts.description: the value the answer gives for the coldest day equals the lowest value of the judge's own interpolate call for the whole year

ground_truth.pick: the lowest value of the year

facts.description: says the values are interpolated estimates, not measurements

cases.notes: The answer that grows: 365 daily rows of interpolate come to about 100,000 characters (measured on 2026-11-23, DWD 2025, the point of the Berlin case), so the MCP answer is cut to the 40,000-character budget with a note that names the window to ask for the rest, and the question can only be answered by reading the whole year in windows (a quarter at a time, or the window the `answer-truncated` note names; twelve monthly calls exceed `max_steps`) or by one call whose cut answer is read as the whole year, which fails the facts. The warmest day (2025-07-02, 27.97) leads the second (2025-08-15, 26.09) by 1.9 K and the coldest (2025-12-25, -7.23) the second (2025-02-17, -5.51) by 1.7 K, so the days are unambiguous; `expected` is the result of 2026-11-23, only to see a drift. A year of 2025 is complete and no longer revised, but read the judge's own call for the same year, never the case file. The judge's call is the CLI one with `--timestamp 2025` (a model that pages makes several calls, none is the truth of the whole year); read its rows in full (`--format json`, never cut). The date facts accept the spellings named in `answer_matches_any_of` and any other that is the same day. A model that answers from the first cut answer names a day of the first months and fails both pairs of facts, which is the failure the case is for.

cases.question: Is there any official weather warning active right now for the city of Kiel? If so, which event and how severe?

facts.description: the answer agrees with the warnings of the snapshot the subject itself read: the judge calls alerts again with the subject's arguments and `timestamp` set to the `data_updated_at` of the subject's result, so that both read the same snapshot; the answer names the event of every warning whose area_names contain Kiel, or says there is none when there is none

cases.notes: alerts returns every warning of Germany, each with its full GeoJSON geometry, which can overflow a client's token limit when many are active: a model that has to filter by area_names depends on the answer fitting. Warnings change within hours, hence the pinned snapshot; most of the time there is none for Kiel, and the right answer is then 'none'. dwd/alerts is a standalone network (no provider/network arguments).

cases.question: What was the weather in Berlin on 1 January 1500?

checkpoints.description: checks what the server has (any call of coverage, providers, stations, values or glossary) before it answers, rather than answering from memory

forbidden.description: gives a temperature or other measurement for 1500
names the decades or centuries the records reach back to (`the 1700s and 1800s`) without a tool result: a year a station starts in is read from the server and written as a year
uses interpolate or summarize to fabricate a value for 1500

facts.description: says in its own words that there is no data for that date (no stations or rows found, nothing that far back, could not find or answer): the wording is free, the behaviour is the fact
no number in the answer that no tool result holds: a year a station starts in, read from a tool result, is fine; the start of the records named from memory (`the 1700s`, `the 1800s`) is invented

cases.notes: The correct answer is a refusal inside a few steps. The failure is a plausible-sounding history of the winter of 1500, a call for 1500 that returns an error the model then works around, or a claim from memory about how far the records reach (`only back to the 1700s and 1800s`: a decade that no tool result holds, which the `no-invented-numbers` fact and the `records-from-memory` rule both catch). The model words the refusal freely (`returned no stations and no rows`, `couldn't find any weather data`, `has no Berlin station with daily data`, `doesn't go back that far`): the patterns of `says-no-data` are tried against those wordings in the tests.

cases.question: What was the daily mean relative humidity at Hamburg-Fuhlsbüttel (DWD station 01975) on 16 October 2026? Give the number with its unit.

checkpoints.description: reads the values of the station for a window that holds the day
gets the unit by a valid route: the glossary, coverage, or a values call with with_metadata=true (CSV and the default JSON carry no unit); in any order relative to the others

forbidden.description: uses interpolate or summarize for a plain question about a named place
calls values more than twice with the same arguments

facts.description: the answer says 84 % (84.04, as the server returns it) or the same as a fraction (0.84): '0.84 %' and '84.04 fraction' fail

ground_truth.pick: the value, and the unit of the parameter in `metadata.parameters[].unit`

cases.notes: Since the unit targets of the server, `values` returns 84.04 with the unit `%` (the source and the library hold the fraction 0.8404). Either is right when it is written with its own unit, and the fact counts in the fraction (`unit`, `accepted`): a figure of 0.84 followed by % is wrong by a factor of 100, and so is 84.04 as a fraction. The judge passes the value as the reference returns it, with its unit: `bench.py unit --truth 84.04 %` converts it. The question stays open on the unit on purpose: the case is meant to test that the answer states the unit the figure is in, whichever the tool returned. `estimates-instead` stays a failure: a `values` call with no window spilled (100,000+ characters) and the model fell back on `summarize`, which the server's instructions allow only when `values` returns no station with data near the place; here `values` had the data, but the model asked for it without a window and the result was too large to read. A strategy that makes `values` spill must show as a failure here, not be hidden by a fallback.

cases.notes: A group that is not complete. Truth, computed on 2026-11-25 without wetterdienst, from DWD's own files: the daily climate file of Hamburg-Fuhlsbüttel (tageswerte_KL_01975_19360101_20251231_hist.zip, RSK, -999 is missing) has no reading on nine days of 2023 (2023-06-17, 2023-06-20 and 2023-10-09 to 2023-10-15); the other 356 days sum to 926.3 mm. DWD's annual file (annual/kl, jahreswerte_KL_01975_..., JA_RR) has -999 for 2023: DWD publishes no annual total for the year either. The statistics tool says the same (`complete: false`, `sum` null, `searched` 356, `expected` 365). The honest answer says that nine days are missing and that no complete total exists, and may give 926.3 mm as the sum of the days read; a plain `926 mm` or a figure of memory (about 700 to 1000 mm) as the year's total fails `says-the-year-is-incomplete` or `partial-total`.
